stage: 1. Target selection and access acquisition (buy from IAB, exploit edge devices, phishing, vishing)
reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Access is a commodity market (median price fell $1,427->$439 in 3yr) and hand-off to the ransomware crew now takes ~22s, so per-victim hours are low though failure rates are high. Open-source recon and target research are strong LLM tasks; buying access and real-time vishing of a help desk are not fully automatable today.
key_sources: Chainalysis 2026; M-Trends 2026; prior-project RANSOM_CARTEL (RC-099); Sophos AA 2026

stage: 2. Foothold, discovery, privilege escalation, lateral movement
reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Largest skilled-labour block and the step agent tools target first. Field use so far is human-supervised and error-prone (Aurora: most agent commands failed first try; PaperCut agents reached RCE in ~4h but ignored exclusion lists). Reaching Active Directory already takes only ~3.4h, so elapsed time is not the constraint. Central ~0.40 of this stage automatable today.
key_sources: Sophos AA 2026 (3.4h to AD); Gambit/Aurora 2026; GreyNoise PaperCut 2026; prior-project RC-100

key_sources: Sophos AA 2026; Coveware Q2 2026; prior-project RC-101

key_sources: Anthropic Aug 2025 (GTG-5004); Sophos AA 2026; prior-project RC-102

stage: 5. Victim research and extortion packaging, leak-site posting
reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Reading and writing - the most natural LLM task. FulcrumSec reportedly used an LLM to analyse stolen data and sharpen demands; DragonForce's 'legal counsel' assessed as LLM-generated. Central ~0.60 automatable.
key_sources: GuidePoint GRIT Q2 2026; prior-project RC-103; Anthropic Aug 2025 (GTG-2002 note drafting)

reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Long and mostly unproductive: ~72-80% of victims never pay (rates at record lows). Chat can be scripted and one gang (Global Group) ran an AI negotiation bot with human review, but whether the victim pays is exogenous to the attacker, so automation cannot lift conversion. This, not intrusion, is the binding constraint on revenue.
key_sources: Coveware Q2 2026; Chainalysis 2026; Axios/Picus (Global Group) 2025; BakerHostetler (8-day negotiations); prior-project RC-104

stage: 7. Payment verification, decryptor, laundering and cash-out, payouts
reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Thin professional layer and the enforcement chokepoint. On-chain movement is automatable but money mules and running-point brokers are 'predominantly manual' per Chainalysis, OTC desks are human relationships, and trust among thieves resists automation. Lowest automatable share.
key_sources: Chainalysis 2026 laundering report; FinCEN 2025; prior-project RC-105

stage: 8. Platform overhead (affiliate panel, tooling, hosting, recruitment)
reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Routine administration borne mostly by brand core staff/suppliers; small share of affiliate hours but larger (~15-25%) of whole-ecosystem hours. Code and admin assistance apply directly.
key_sources: Prior-project RC-106; Conti/LockBit leak structure (NCA; Wired)

reasoning: JUDGEMENT. Steps 1-4 (~65% of affiliate hours) are the most automatable; if fully automated the labour speed-up ceiling is ~2.9x (prior-project central ceiling 3.3x by 2029). But revenue does not scale with intrusions: conversion to payment is demand-limited (payment rate 20-28% and falling) and laundering/cash-out stay human. So AI mainly lowers entry barriers and raises victim counts (observed since 2023) rather than total revenue. 'Most of a heist is still manual' where it matters most - negotiation and money-out.
